data.title: Anthropic founders mint $1.95B from record-breaking IPO
data.description:
Anthropic’s (ANT) seven founders raised $1.95B from the shares they sold in the $100B plus IPO on Thursday.

Each founder sold 3.4 million shares, generating well over $250M at the upgraded price of $83 per share.

Anthropic said that each of the founders has pledged 80% of their personal equity to philanthropy, though the commitments are “voluntary, revocable expressions of each co-founder’s philanthropic intent and do not constitute legally binding obligations.”

The company raised $104.8B in its offering, with Nvidia (NVDA) buying $10B of Class N shares, Google (GOOG) (GOOGL) $10B, and AMD (AMD), Broadcom (AVGO), Micron (MU), Microsoft (MSFT), and TSMC (TSM) the remainder.

Amazon (AMZN) and Google now own 28% of Anthropic.

The AI company’s shares are currently down 5% ahead of its second day of trading, amid a broad AI market selloff.

data.title: Fermi shareholder Toby Neugebauer to appeal dismissal of challenge to 70% bylaw
data.description:
Toby Neugebauer, Fermi Inc.’s (FRMI) co-founder and largest shareholder, said Nov. 19 that he plans to appeal a Texas Business Court ruling dismissing his claims against the company. Shares of the data center real estate investment company closed down 16% on Thursday. 

The lawsuit challenged a bylaw amendment adopted by Fermi’s board in May that requires shareholders to approve certain changes with 70% of all outstanding shares.

The amendment requires that threshold to expand the board or change the process for amending the bylaws. The board can make changes to those rules with a simple majority vote of directors, according to Neugebauer’s statement.

He said the amendment was adopted during a shareholder contest and without a shareholder vote. Fermi’s board also changed director elections in August to require the support of a majority of all outstanding shares, with unvoted shares counted as votes against.

At the company’s Oct. 30 annual meeting, neither of the two directors on the ballot reached that threshold. Both remain on the board, the release said. “Directors who could not win a majority of the shareholder support are still sitting in the boardroom,” Neugebauer said.

He said the court’s ruling gives shareholders a higher threshold to change the bylaws than the board faces when changing them, and said he disagrees with the decision and intends to appeal.

data.title: India eyes 162.5% Scotch duty, testing U.K.-India trade pact - Reuters
data.description:
Just months after coming into force, the India-U.K. trade agreement is reportedly facing its first major challenge, with New Delhi opposing the extension of preferential tariff rates to bulk Scotch whisky imports.

Duty on bulk Scotch whisky imports was expected to be slashed to 75% and then gradually to 40% over 10 years as per the trade agreement. However, a Reuters report Thursday said that India now plans to levy a 162.5% duty on these imports, higher than the 150% in place before the trade deal.

Amid the confusion over tax rates, thousands of liters of bulk Scotch in more than 80 shipping containers belonging to Pernod, Diageo, and Bacardi are stuck at Indian ports, according to Reuters.

But in the first major dispute linked to the India-UK pact, Indian investigators have argued companies are using wrong customs classifications in importing bulk Scotch concentrates - these are deemed to be raw material used to make drinks like blended whiskies.

Since May, such imports, Indian ​investigators argue, come under a newly created customs line for so-called “compound alcoholic preparations", which attracts a 150% tariff, the report said. These imports then attract a consumption tax, which takes the full duty amount to 162.5%, ​according to a government document reviewed by Reuters and sources.

Under a so-called provisional release pending investigation, duty at ​75% of the goods’ value needs to be paid up front, with the rest covered by bank guarantees, the sources said.

"Industry has already reduced prices of Scotch products in the market when the India-UK pact kicked ​in, and now they are faced with higher duties again," said a source in the liquor importing business.

Pernod, which owns UK-based Chivas Brothers, Diageo, and many other Indian companies, believes Scotch imports - bulk and bottled both - should be taxed only at 75% as per the trade pact.

The British government has repeatedly said in statements it is working with New Delhi on the issue, while India has said the dispute will be resolved soon, the report added.

Elsewhere, the top-selling American whiskey brands include Brown-Forman's (BF.A) (BF.B) Jack Daniel's, Woodford Reserve, Old Forester, and Jack Daniel's Tennessee Honey, as well as Suntory's (STBFY) Jim Beam and Maker's Mark, Heaven Hill Brands' Evan Williams, Campari Group's (DVDCF) Wild Turkey, Diageo's (DEO) Bulleit, and Sazerac's Buffalo Trace.

data.title: Esco outlines FY 2027 sales of $2.05B-$2.09B and adjusted EPS of $9.40-$9.70 backed by Megger integration
data.description:
Earnings Call Insights: ESCO Technologies (ESE) Q4 2026

Management View

  • "Momentum remained positive across all business segments in Q4 with broad-based order strength from all business platforms" (President, CEO & Director Bryan Sayler). "Strong demand throughout the year drove a book-to-bill ratio above 1 in every quarter and 1.31 for the full year" and "We ended the fiscal year with record orders and backlog" (President, CEO & Director Sayler).
  • "During the year, we also took a transformational step in ESCO's growth with the addition of Megger Group Limited, the largest acquisition in our history" (President, CEO & Director Sayler). "The combined company will now be known as Doble and Megger" and management said the integration planning and "cost reduction actions" began immediately after close (President, CEO & Director Sayler).
  • "Strong order activity across both Navy businesses drove their combined backlog to more than $770 million, up over 40% from the prior year" (President, CEO & Director Sayler). "Commercial aerospace sales were strong throughout the year and grew 20% year-over-year" while "Our teams in the aircraft business continue to manage a number of supply chain and capacity challenges" (President, CEO & Director Sayler).
  • "ESCO's fourth quarter performance was strong" (Senior VP & CFO Christopher Tucker). "Orders increased 22% compared to last year's fourth quarter" and "Sales increased by 9%, which was all organic growth" (Senior VP & CFO Tucker).

Outlook

  • "We expect organic growth in the range of 7% to 9% in 2027, and we expect Megger sales in the range of $640 million to $660 million" (Senior VP & CFO Tucker). "This results in a consolidated sales expectation within a range of $2.05 billion to $2.09 billion" (Senior VP & CFO Tucker).
  • "We expect adjusted EBIT dollars to increase between 51% to 55% with margins in the range of 21.2% to 21.8%" (Senior VP & CFO Tucker). "[T]hat get us to an adjusted earnings per share range of $9.40 to $9.70" and the company emphasized these are "adjusted earnings" that "will exclude some sizable costs related to the closing of the Megger transaction as well as integration expenses and acquisition-related amortization" (Senior VP & CFO Tucker).
  • On Megger synergies, "the guidance includes $20 million in synergies for 2027" (President, CEO & Director Sayler). "[W]e feel very, very confident in being able to achieve that number" (President, CEO & Director Sayler).

Financial Results

  • "Adjusted EBIT margins were 24.1% and adjusted earnings per share finished at $2.67" in Q4 (Senior VP & CFO Tucker).
  • Aerospace & Defense Q4 included "sales in the quarter were $190 million" and "backlog of $1.1 billion" (Senior VP & CFO Tucker). "On the profitability side, we had good improvement to 29.7% adjusted EBIT margins" (Senior VP & CFO Tucker).
  • Utility Solutions Group Q4 had "NRG sales in the quarter declined by 20%" and management said it "expect[s] the business to stabilize going forward" (Senior VP & CFO Tucker).
  • Full-year results included "Sales have also been strong with 21% growth to just over $1.3 billion" and "adjusted earnings per share was $8.42" (Senior VP & CFO Tucker). "Operating cash flow was up significantly at over $295 million compared to $200 million in the prior year" (Senior VP & CFO Tucker).

Q&A

  • Scott Deuschle, Deutsche Bank AG, Research Division: "can you share any type of guidance goalposts for margins by segment in 2027?" Christopher Tucker: "Aerospace & Defense, we're a little ahead of the 30% target" and "Test, we're, kind of, right at that 30% range on incrementals" while utility is "a little bit complicated there with Megger coming in" (Senior VP & CFO Tucker).
  • Scott Deuschle, Deutsche Bank AG, Research Division: asked about Doble "unfavorable mix and production cost increases" and expectations into 2027. Christopher Tucker: "we did see material cost escalation" including "electronic components" and "steel and copper" and cited a Q4 revenue shortfall where "another $3 million to $4 million of revenue" shifted into "past due backlog" (Senior VP & CFO Tucker).
  • Tomohiko Sano, JPMorgan Chase & Co, Research Division: asked about excluded Megger costs. Christopher Tucker: deal costs "will be around $20 million" plus "transfer taxes... around $10 million" and "integration costs" with "that number to be around $30 million as a P&L impact" (Senior VP & CFO Tucker).
  • Tomohiko Sano, JPMorgan Chase & Co, Research Division: asked about potential data center project delays. Bryan Sayler: "we have indirect exposure" and direct exposure is "maybe 1% to 2% of the total revenue for Doble-Megger" and "we're not anticipating any substantial reduction in our 2027 outlook" (President, CEO & Director Sayler).
  • Jonathan Tanwanteng, CJS Securities, Inc.: asked if election results changed planning. Bryan Sayler: "no, we did not bake any changes based on the election into our 2027 guidance" and said shipbuilding programs have "good bipartisan support" (President, CEO & Director Sayler).
  • Jonathan Tanwanteng, CJS Securities, Inc.: asked about revenue synergies from the Megger combination. Bryan Sayler: "No, we did not include any revenue synergies in the guide" and said it is "a little bit too early" (President, CEO & Director Sayler).
  • Scott Deuschle, Deutsche Bank AG, Research Division: asked about 737 and Virginia-class build-rate alignment. Bryan Sayler: "what we're seeing out of our customer there is consistent with our expectations" and for Virginia-class, "we generally are building 1 or 2 vessels ahead of where the shipyard is" (President, CEO & Director Sayler).
  • Scott Deuschle, Deutsche Bank AG, Research Division: asked free cash flow conversion for 2027. Christopher Tucker: "we expect it to normalize back a little bit" after "really big advanced payments" on Navy programs (Senior VP & CFO Tucker).

Sentiment Analysis

  • Analysts were slightly negative to neutral, pressing on what was excluded from guidance and on cost/mix issues, including "How much visibility do you have today" on integration costs and "what exactly drove those mix and cost pressures" at Doble (Tomohiko Sano, JPMorgan Chase & Co, Research Division; Scott Deuschle, Deutsche Bank AG, Research Division).
  • Management tone was positive and confident on integration and FY 2027 execution, including "we feel very, very confident" on "$20 million in synergies for 2027" (President, CEO & Director Sayler), while acknowledging uncertainty on timing/size of integration costs: "there's still, kind of, a lot of moving parts" (Senior VP & CFO Tucker).
  • Versus Q3, management language shifted from anticipating closing timing to executing post-close actions, moving from "expected to close in the first quarter of fiscal 2027" (President, CEO & Director Sayler, Q3) to "completed the transaction" and "right on day 1" restructuring actions (President, CEO & Director Sayler, Q4).

Quarter-over-quarter Comparison

  • Guidance expanded from Q3’s raised FY 2026 range of "$8.30 to $8.40" adjusted EPS (Senior VP & CFO Tucker, Q3) to an initial FY 2027 adjusted EPS range of "$9.40 to $9.70" and consolidated sales of "$2.05 billion to $2.09 billion" (Senior VP & CFO Tucker, Q4), explicitly including Megger in Q4.
  • Megger discussion moved from regulatory process and planning ("tracking to our expectations") in Q3 to closed-deal execution in Q4, including naming the combined platform "Doble and Megger" and detailing synergy timing with "$20 million" embedded in FY 2027 (President, CEO & Director Sayler).
  • Utility discussion shifted from Q3’s Doble-led strength with renewables softness to Q4’s sharper disclosure on NRG ("declined by 20%") and margin pressure linked to "volume deleverage" and Doble cost escalation (Senior VP & CFO Tucker).

Risks and Concerns

  • Integration-related costs and uncertainty remained a key near-term item: "integration costs... around $30 million as a P&L impact" with potential movement, and amortization still being "work[ed] through" (Senior VP & CFO Tucker).
  • Utility margin and execution risks centered on NRG weakness and Doble supply chain/approvals: Doble had "past due backlog" tied to "supply chain challenges and some customer approvals" (Senior VP & CFO Tucker).
  • Aerospace operational constraints were flagged as ongoing: "supply chain and capacity challenges" in the aircraft business (President, CEO & Director Sayler).

Final Takeaway

ESCO’s FY 2027 framework emphasized a larger revenue base and earnings growth with Megger included, alongside a defined first-year synergy target of $20 million and an adjusted EPS range of $9.40 to $9.70. Management highlighted record orders and backlog exiting FY 2026, but acknowledged near-term pressure points in Utility Solutions from NRG volume deleverage, Doble material costs, and integration-related expenses that will be excluded from adjusted results and updated over coming quarters.

data.title: Asian stocks slump on Wall Street decline, PBoC rate hold, hotter Japan inflation, and muted Xi-Trump-Putin summit
data.description:
Asian equity markets traded sharply lower on Friday, tracking overnight losses on Wall Street as Anthropic’s record-breaking market debut failed to ease broader concerns surrounding the artificial intelligence trade.

Japan’s Nikkei 225 (NKY:IND) fell 4.90% to 56,517.50 level, with the Japanese yen appreciated toward 159 per dollar. South Korea’s benchmark KOSPI fell 5.72% to around 4,843.97. The South Korean won weakened to around 1,337 per dollar. Meanwhile, Hong Kong’s Hang Seng Index (HSI) fell 2.39%, to around 22,294.50, and mainland China’s Shanghai Composite (SHCOMP) fell 2.00% to 3,506.03, while the Shenzhen Component fell 2.57% to 10,311.66. Australia’s S&P/ASX 200 (AS51) fell 1.58%, to 8,592.60.

The People's Bank of China (PBoC) left its key lending rates unchanged at record lows for the 18th consecutive month, holding the one-year LPR at 3.0% and the five-year LPR at 3.5%. 

Meanwhile, Japan’s annual inflation accelerated to 2.3% in October from 2.1% in September (an 11-month high), with core CPI rising to 2.2% Y/Y and food inflation easing to 2.7%.

Investors found few catalysts in a trilateral meeting between Presidents Xi Jinping, Donald Trump, and Vladimir Putin. While Beijing and Moscow noted broad alignment on UN reform, refined petroleum supply, International Criminal Court overreach, and nuclear risk reduction, a Kremlin aide indicated that a separate bilateral discussion between Trump and Putin regarding the war in Ukraine yielded no significant statements.

In commodities and crypto, gold prices retreated toward $3,500 an ounce, while crude oil climbed toward $83 per barrel.

Wall Street closed lower on Thursday, with U.S. futures dipping on Friday, as Anthropic’s blockbuster market debut fell short of calming wider artificial intelligence sector jitters.

data.title: White House names Kirsten Davies as cyber chief after outages hit MSFT, banks
data.description:
The White House appointed a new national cyber director on Thursday, following a series of widespread service disruptions that affected daily life and raised concerns among Americans.

Kirsten Davies, chief information officer at the Defense Department, will fill the role, according to social media posts by several members of Trump's cabinet. She will replace Sean Cairncross as the administration's top cybersecurity official.

“Our nation stands in the crossroad of analog, digital, and quantum technologies, our American way of living increasingly interconnected,” Davies wrote in a post on X. “Our opportunity is to dominate the cyber landscape for generations to come … but only if we modernize and drive resilience into the foundations our great nation runs on, as well as build cyber talent for our future.”

President Donald Trump faced a groundswell of criticism as Americans grappled with a cascade of service outages that snarled travel, cut off work, limited bank access, and disrupted classified communications.

Even staunch Trump allies accused the administration of lying to Americans or hiding information about the true cause of the disruptions. Over the past week, Microsoft (MSFT), Chase Bank, air traffic control, and the National Security Agency have all been affected.

Secretary of State Marco Rubio on Tuesday sought to assure Americans that there’s “zero” information that the technical failures are related to each other or to a malign actor.

The White House made the change as Trump returned from a three-day trip to Asia, where he downplayed the episodes, declaring that “things like that happen.”

“She has proven herself to be a dedicated patriot and professional, and we are confident she will advance President Trump’s America First agenda across the cybersecurity landscape,” Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth wrote in a post on X congratulating Davies.

The AP contributed to this report.

data.title: Mutual Federal Bancorp's successor, MFB Bancorp launches stock offering of up to 1.04M shares at $10/share
data.description:
Mutual Federal Bancorp (MFDB) announced that MFB Bancorp, Inc., the newly formed Delaware corporation and proposed successor holding company for Mutual Federal Bank, has commenced its stock offering as part of the conversion of Mutual Federal Bancorp, MHC from a mutual holding company to a stock holding company structure.

MFB Bancorp is offering up to 1.04M common shares (adjustable up to 1.19M shares) at $10.00 per share, with a minimum threshold of 765K  shares required to complete the transaction.

Shares are initially offered to eligible depositors (as of March 31, 2025), benefit plans, and certain borrowers.

Unsubscribed shares may be sold in a community offering, giving first preference to Cook County, Illinois residents and second preference to existing Mutual Federal Bancorp stockholders of record as of November 9, 2026.

Following completion, MFB Bancorp's common stock is expected to trade on the OTCQB Market under the symbol "MFDB."

Closing remains subject to final regulatory approvals, stockholder and MHC member sign-offs, and meeting the minimum share sale requirement.
